title: Polynomial specialization of groupoid norms after arbitrary invariant-base extension
statement:
Let $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $R=\operatorname{Spec}B$ be affine schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $s,t:R\to U$, $e:U\to R$, $i:R\to R$, and $c:R\times_{s,U,t}R\to R$ [def-pc-fibre-product] define a groupoid: functorially in every test scheme $H$, they make $U(H)$ the objects and $R(H)$ the arrows with source $s$, target $t$, identity $e$, inverse $i$, and composition $c$. Assume $s,t$ are finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Write $\sigma=s^\sharp,\tau=t^\sharp:A\to B$. Put $C=\{a\in A:\sigma(a)=\tau(a)\}$ and let $d:C\to D$ be any homomorphism of commutative rings. With the common $C$-algebra structure on $B$, set $A_D=A\otimes_C D$, $B_D=B\otimes_C D$ [def-weil-module-base-change], $\sigma_D=\sigma\otimes1$, $\tau_D=\tau\otimes1$, and $\eta_D:D\to A_D$, $x\mapsto1\otimes x$. The groupoid structure maps are morphisms over $\operatorname{Spec}C$; their base changes along $\operatorname{Spec}D\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ are morphisms over $\operatorname{Spec}D$ that define a groupoid on $\operatorname{Spec}B_D\rightrightarrows\operatorname{Spec}A_D$, functorially in every test scheme over $\operatorname{Spec}D$, with source $\operatorname{Spec}\sigma_D$ and target $\operatorname{Spec}\tau_D$, and this source and target are finite locally free. Norms mean the locally glued multiplication determinants of [lem-pd-finite-locally-free-norm-charts, def-weil-endomorphism-determinant]. For every $f\in A_D$ and every expression $f=\sum_{j=1}^m a_j\otimes d_j$ (including $m=0$), form $F=\sum_j a_jT_j$ in $A[T_1,\ldots,T_m]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. The norm for the coefficientwise polynomial extensions satisfies
$$G=N_{\sigma[T]}(\tau[T](F))\in C[T_1,\ldots,T_m],\qquad N_{\sigma_D}(\tau_D(f))=\eta_D\bigl(d[T](G)(d_1,\ldots,d_m)\bigr).$$
Here $d[T]$ applies $d$ to the coefficients and evaluation sends $T_j$ to $d_j$. In particular, the latter norm belongs to the image of $\eta_D$, even when $d$ is not flat. For every algebraically closed field $k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure], every $d:C\to k$ and any two $k$-algebra maps $\alpha_0,\alpha_1:A_k\to k$, all these norms have equal values under $\alpha_0$ and $\alpha_1$. No constant-rank, reducedness or global freeness hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Let $q_U:U\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ be induced by the inclusion, and set $q_R=q_U\circ s=q_U\circ t$; the equality is exactly $\sigma|_C=\tau|_C$. The groupoid identities give $q_R\circ e=q_U$, $q_R\circ i=q_R$, and $q_R\circ c=q_R\circ p_1$ on $P=R\times_{s,U,t}R$. Moreover $q_R\circ p_0=q_U\circ s\circ p_0=q_U\circ t\circ p_1=q_R\circ p_1$. Thus every structure map is over $\operatorname{Spec}C$, including composition with the indicated structure map on $P$. These are identities of morphisms, since the assumed functorial groupoid laws hold on every test scheme.

source.place: Tag 03BK (groupoids-lemma-invariants-base-change)(1), explicit verification that the structure maps are over the invariant base

proof.text: Use the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] to base change these maps along $\operatorname{Spec}D\to\operatorname{Spec}C$. For any $H\to\operatorname{Spec}D$, a map $H\to U_D$ over $D$ is exactly a map $H\to U$ over $C$, and likewise for $R$ and $P$. Under these identifications, $P_D$ represents pairs of arrows in $R_D(H)$ with matching source and target, hence $P_D=R_D\times_{s_D,U_D,t_D}R_D$ canonically. The operations on these pairs are the original operations, and every identity, inverse and associativity law is therefore the original law on $H$. This proves the groupoid assertion on every test scheme over $D$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $U_D=\operatorname{Spec}A_D$ and $R_D=\operatorname{Spec}B_D$; their source and target maps on rings send $a\otimes z$ to $\sigma(a)\otimes z$ and $\tau(a)\otimes z$.

source.place: Tag 03BK(1), filling the omitted proof by the fibre-product universal property

proof.text: The squares for $s_D$ and $t_D$ over $s$ and $t$ are cartesian: a map to either corner is just the compatible pair of maps used in step 2. Consequently both maps are finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](a), flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change], and locally of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3). By [def-pc-finite-locally-free] they are finite locally free. This argument applies to every $C$-algebra, including $C[T_1,\ldots,T_m]$; no flatness of the base algebra was used.

proof.text:
Define $\phi_A:A[\mathbf T]	o A_D$ by $a\mapsto a\otimes1$, $T_j\mapsto1\otimes d_j$, and $\phi_B:B[\mathbf T]	o B_D$ by the corresponding formulas. These are evaluation homomorphisms by [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], and they commute with $\sigma,	au$. In particular $\phi_A(F)=f$ and $\phi_B(	au[\mathbf T](F))=	au_D(f)$. The source square is a scalar-extension square: the explicit isomorphism
$$B[\mathbf T]\otimes_{A[\mathbf T]}A_D\longrightarrow B_D$$
sends $(b\mathbf T^
u)\otimes(a\otimes z)$ to $b\sigma(a)\otimes d^
u z$, where $d^
u=\prod_jd_j^{
u_j}$. Its inverse sends $b\otimes z$ to $b\otimes(1\otimes z)$. The balancing relations over $C$ and $A[\mathbf T]$ make these maps well defined and make both composites identities; moving $T_j$ to the second factor gives $1\otimes d_j$ there. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] this is also the cartesian square of affine schemes needed to pull back local norm charts.

source.place: Tag 02DV (exercises-exercise-trace-det-rings)(3), specialization map and explicit scalar-extension identification

proof.text: Take an affine norm chart $V\subset\operatorname{Spec}(A[\mathbf T])$ from [lem-pd-finite-locally-free-norm-charts], with coordinate ring $E$ and arrow algebra $L$ free on $e_1,\ldots,e_r$. Put $b=\tau[\mathbf T](F)|_V$ and write $be_j=\sum_i M_{ij}e_i$. Its norm is $G|_V=\det M$ by [def-weil-endomorphism-determinant]. The inverse image $W$ of $V$ in $\operatorname{Spec}A_D$ is affine and its arrow algebra is $L\otimes_E E'$, $E'=\Gamma(W,\mathcal O)$, by the cartesian square of step 5 and [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. The basis after extension is $e_j\otimes1$: the coordinates of $\sum_j e_j\otimes z_j$ are $(z_j)_j$, inverse to $(z_j)_j\mapsto\sum_j e_j\otimes z_j$, by [def-weil-module-base-change]. Multiplication by the image of $b$, which is $\tau_D(f)|_W$, has matrix $(h(M_{ij}))$, where $h:E\to E'$ is the restriction of $\phi_A$. The determinant formula [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant] gives $\det(h(M_{ij}))=h(\det M)$, since a ring map preserves every signed product and finite sum. Thus the local norm of $\tau_D(f)$ equals $\phi_A(G)$ on $W$. The arrow schemes over these affine charts are affine by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](b), so the section-algebra identifications apply.

The inverse images $W$ of the norm charts cover $\operatorname{Spec}A_D$. On each of them the norm specified in the statement is the multiplication determinant, so step 6 and the sheaf equality axiom give $N_{\sigma_D}(	au_D(f))=\phi_A(G)$ globally. Since $G=\sum_

The middle equality is the defining $C$-tensor relation [def-weil-module-base-change]. This proves the formula and its scalar-image consequence for every chosen expression of $f$. For $m=0$ the polynomial ring has just its constant monomial, $F=0$, and all the displayed evaluation and tensor formulas have their usual empty-sum or empty-product meanings. The matrix proof also allows rank zero charts and different ranks on different charts, without dividing by anything.

proof.text: Finally put $D=k$. For any $f\in A_k$ and its chosen tensor expression, let $z=d[\mathbf T](G)(d_1,\ldots,d_m)\in k$. Step 7 gives $N_{\sigma_k}(\tau_k(f))=\eta_k(z)$. As $\alpha_0,\alpha_1$ are $k$-algebra maps, $\alpha_0(\eta_k(z))=z=\alpha_1(\eta_k(z))$. Thus the two values agree for all these norms. This last argument works over any field; algebraic closedness is the hypothesis required in the geometric-point application, rather than an additional property used in the calculation.
